catalog_quote: c) It contains one and only one vowel which is distinctly more prominent in loudness and pitch than any of the other vowels in the word, and is here called "stressed". Typically, this vowel is the last full vowel of the form, i.e. any vowel except /ə/. If the last vowel is /ə/, the preceding full vowel is stressed. A short vowel in word-final position is never stressed. When a word ends in a short vowel, the full vowel immediately preceding it is the stressed one. Thus, given words of the structure, CVCV·, CVCVC, CVCVCəC, CVCVCəCa, they are predictably stressed CVCV́·, CVCV́C, CVCV́CəC, CVCV́CəCa. Only a very few words do not conform to this pattern and are found to contain the juncture phoneme /+/ (see 160, 856, and 857.2). ... 131 Stress. Diegueño is a strongly stressed language, but stress is not phonemic since its placement within the word is predictable. ... [p. 89, sec. 310] Every…

sources.quote: 'For the related Jamul variety, Miller (2001) states that stress is predictable and non-contrastive, coextensive with a morphological root posited for all Yuman languages (Miller 2001; see also Langdon 1970). In Ja'a Kumiai, stress is similarly morphophonologically predictable: it coincides with the morphological root ... The stressed syllable occurs word-finally excluding enclitics such as tag question marker =keʔe and demonstrative marker =pe. ...
